0.content:
The Tianquan of the Qixing and Keqing's opposite in temperament. Keqing once saw her as treating Liyue Harbor as a marketplace whose only principle was profit, and grumbled that the Tianquan, who should enforce the rules on people like Beidou, is always too busy. After Rex Lapis's departure they found common ground; Keqing now counts her "a comrade in arms" while disagreeing on many issues. Keqing told the Traveler in 1.0 that her scepticism of the adepti was her own and that Ningguang did not share it.

Petty friction remains: Ningguang bought up months of Lucent Crescent jewellery at double price, robbing Keqing of a pre-order. Ningguang urges Keqing to rest and to show the public a new look at festivals; Keqing's 2.4 Lantern Rite dress came from Ningguang's tailor. Ningguang says Keqing "has changed a lot recently" and wonders which Yuheng is better for Liyue.

1.content:
Ganyu, the half-adeptus secretary who serves both Keqing and Ningguang, carries out Keqing's instructions to the letter even when she has doubts. Keqing used to wonder what Rex Lapis had done to earn such blind devotion, and spoke ill of him in front of her. Now Keqing consults her constantly as the person in Liyue most familiar with Rex Lapis's ways, a little awkwardly. Ganyu once could not stand Keqing's irreverence; Rex Lapis told her "this is just the kind of person Liyue needs". Watching Keqing restart the Bishui trade-route plan again and again, Ganyu began to understand her.

Keqing protects Ganyu from overwork, covering for her before Cloud Retainer (2.4, limited) and refusing to let her work two days without sleep (3.4, limited). Paimon points out the irony of that. Ganyu fetched Baizhu when Keqing sprained her ankle (5.4).

2.comment: Keqing: Rex Lapis and the Rite of Descension speech
2.content:
Keqing once questioned Rex Lapis openly. "Does Morax really know everything?" she asked, and argued that issues affecting humans should be handled by humans. At a Rite of Descension she asked how long the status quo could last: "Rex Lapis has watched over Liyue for a millennium. But what about the next millennium?" The god burst into hearty laughter. Some devotees grumbled; she considered them complacent.

After his "death" she took on his duties and was humbled. She keeps a whole shelf of Rex Lapis figurines "for self-reflection", asks herself "What would Rex Lapis do?", and has come to believe his laughter was acknowledgement and expectation. She vows to catch up with him. In truth Rex Lapis is Zhongli, who says the most impious Qixing is the kind of person who let him step back. He even wonders if the plan to take power from gods and adepti was originally hers. Keqing does not know any of this.

3.content: To Keqing, Zhongli is the learned consultant of Wangsheng Funeral Parlor who helped organise the Rite of Parting. She respects him but finds him too traditional, thinking "in the same tired old terms as Rex Lapis did", and wishes he were more original so he could help her. She is the only character unaware of his identity who openly compares him to Rex Lapis. She thanked him for his help at the Rite and urged him not to miss the 2.4 fireworks.

4.content:
Keqing met the Traveler at the repaired Guizhong Ballista on Mt. Tianheng, and they impressed her as a good listener. After the battle with Osial she publicly offered them any reward, and was taken aback when they only wanted help posting notices for their missing sibling. She likes that the Traveler makes up their own mind about gods, asks people to be blunt with her, and admits the Traveler's opinion is the one that might make her think twice. She has made them promise to visit when the new Liyue Harbor is born.

She jokes that the Traveler is "the person of my dreams", meaning a crucial part of her plans for Liyue. In the Serenitea Pot she surveys the realm, critiques its land-use planning and invites the Traveler stargazing as a reward for work done. She brought the Traveler along on festival errands (2.4) and on investigations (2.1, 6.3).

5.comment: Keqing: Battle against Osial and the Rite of Parting
5.content: In Chapter I Act III (1.0), Keqing investigated the Guizhong Ballista's mysterious overnight repair, a mystery even to the Qixing. While the Qixing and adepti were at odds over Rex Lapis's death, she called the adepti's protection "sanctimonious arrogance". She said the time of the adepti had passed, yet admitted they had shown restraint. When Childe freed Osial, Keqing led the Millelith to defend the replicated ballistas against Fatui attackers while three adepti fired. Ningguang finally dropped the Jade Chamber on the god. At the Rite of Parting, Keqing observed that every nation has scars from the past, and offered the Traveler a reward.

6.comment: Keqing: Moonlight Merriment and the Stove God
6.content: During a limited-time Moonchase event (2.1), Keqing took custody of a smooth, unbreakable stone that a fishing crew had found. She suspected it was the lost shrine stone of the Stove God, whose tribute her grandfather thought was the forerunner of the Moonchase Festival. She judged the Masterful Chefs cook-off, voted for Smiley Yanxiao's dish (with Golden Shrimp Balls) over her friend Xiangling's, and then agonised over telling her. Xiangling cooked Chili-Mince Cornbread Buns from her grandfather's damaged notes, and the taste took Keqing back to her childhood. The stone then burst open to reveal a statue resembling Guoba, and Madame Ping explained that Guoba is the Stove God, who had surrendered his power to the soil. Keqing said Xiangling might be the first to give the Stove God the experience of a satisfied customer.

7.content: A well-known Liyue real estate tycoon and scholar who collected old books and studied lost customs. He read the classics with young Keqing, debating how much was true and whether Rex Lapis was real. He told her that books are only a bridge to history and that later generations must ask the questions and decide what the answers mean. His advice "In contests of food, always follow your heart" still guides her. Madame Ping knew him and says he was bold and diligent, just like her. His family had academic ties with Yelan's ancestors. He has died; Keqing inherited his notes and unfinished questions.

8.comment: Keqing: The Vision Keqing tried to destroy
8.content: Keqing once saw her Electro Vision as a challenge and an insult from the gods, since people credited the Vision for what she had earned by hard work. She burned it for three days and nights, ran a minecart of rocks over it and threw it from the Jade Chamber; it survived everything. Not wanting it in the wrong hands, she kept it, realised it carried no divine will and had many uses, and adopted it. She is glad she failed. Her equally weathered hairpin, charged with Electro, is her all-purpose survival tool, and she takes pride in its wear: "Its weathered form is what gives it its charm."

key: The Crane Returns on the Wind
9.comment: Keqing: Beisht and the Jade Chamber's return
9.content: In the 2.4 Interlude (The Crane Returns on the Wind), the rebuilt Jade Chamber's rise drew out Beisht, Osial's vengeful remnant. Keqing commanded the barrage ("Fire!"). Afterwards she reported Millelith casualties within expectations, noted that a barrier against the waves would have helped, and resolved never to repeat the mistakes, thanking the Traveler for their help.

10.comment: Keqing: Lantern Rite 2022 (Fleeting Colors in Flight)
10.content: During a limited-time Lantern Rite (2.4), Keqing ran the fireworks plan. She insisted the show be visible across Liyue, including Qingce Village, and told her aide Pengyi that a budget exists to achieve the goal, not the other way round. She asked the Traveler to introduce her to the adepti so she could deliver festive gifts on the Qixing's behalf. She took Madame Ping silks and hand-picked flower seeds, and gave Cloud Retainer a modified firework launcher, carefully bringing no snacks because Cloud Retainer is picky about food. Then Shenhe arrived with food and was welcomed. She also met Xiao at Wangshu Inn, tracked stolen fireworks to a Treasure Hoarder stash near Qingce Village and made the thieves surrender. For this Lantern Rite she wore a formal dress (Opulent Splendor) as a symbol of balancing work and life, then overworked herself anyway.

key: Vibrant Harriers Aloft in Spring Breeze
11.content: In The Exquisite Night Chimes (3.4), the Qixing approved Ganyu's proposal for a Lantern Rite concert. Keqing worked with the composer Dvorak to organise it and called herself "an avid supporter of all things new and innovative". She praised Madame Ping's wisdom whatever form she takes. In Duel! The Summoners' Summit! (3.7) she said practically everyone at Yujing Terrace plays Genius Invokation TCG, offered Kazuha a match, had a deck arranged for him and alerted the Millelith about a card thief. She also appears in the 4.4 Lantern Rite event.

12.comment: Keqing: Springtime Charms and the Eight Adepts
12.content: At the 5.3 Lantern Rite (limited event), Keqing introduced Lan Yan's rattan-figure game "Immortal Combat". She recounted the legend of the Eight Adepts who purified the tree-god Tao Dou, whose remains became the border between life and death. She named the Guizang Hermits (Wind Reader, the Yunlai Angler, the Wuwang Kid), the Two Sages of Lianshan and the Three Beasts of Tao Dou. When a crisis struck during the festival, she held the Gate of Life at Yilong Wharf in the Seven-and-Eight-Gates Method, using its power and Hu Tao's rattan figure to take part of the "fetor blast" off Hu Tao. Afterwards she joked to Ganyu that Ningguang "made the whole thing up", then explained that an untraceable letter had supplied it, and led Ganyu to conclude it could only have come from Xianyun and her friends.

13.content: At the 6.3 Lantern Rite (A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon, limited event), Keqing, Ningguang and Lan Yan confirmed that the legendary "Zhanzhu the Moon-Devourer" phenomenon had really occurred and would recur. Keqing traced a disturbed diner, Lu Xiangxiang, to an excavation in the Chasm funded by Huishan Hall and sent her to Baizhu. She had personally reviewed the excavated artifacts for the Ministry of Civil Affairs; they repeatedly mention jade, which she linked to the ancient nation of Lang-Gan, and use ceremonial language for worshipping the moon and gods. The Traveler brought her a photograph of the moon going dark over Chiwang Terrace; she took it to Cloud Retainer, asking whether it related to the Moonchase Rite, and Ganyu credits that visit with revealing the connection. Later she watched the eclipse alongside the others.

14.content: The Traveler meets Keqing at Bubu Pharmacy. She sprained her ankle descending a mountain while distracted, ignored it until she could not walk, and needed Ganyu to fetch Baizhu. Now nearly recovered, she is collecting nourishing herbs and insists that scrapes and bruises from almost daily land surveys are no big deal. Baizhu's verdict elsewhere: she is ambitious enough to trade her health for her career and would not listen to him anyway.
